<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Long multimodal requests retain raw CPU inputs in every MRV2 worker during decoding, even after those inputs have been consumed. Release the request-local worker inputs after confirmed consumption while preserving EngineCore replay data.

The optional node-local COW tensor transport has been extracted into [a separate branch](https://github.com/Sy0307/vllm/tree/sy03/pr57368-shared-storage-20261012). This PR now contains only the scheduler/worker lifetime protocol and its tests/documentation, following the split requested in review.

## Claims

- Release consumed worker CPU input data by request ID and input index while retaining feature metadata and GPU encoder outputs.
- Account for in-flight prefill and speculative lookahead; reset tracking on preemption/resume/streaming installation and completion.
- Restore previously released inputs when KV-load rollback schedules encoding again. EngineCore keeps replayable inputs; address-only processor-cache SHM handles keep their separate ownership protocol.

## Validation

Rebased onto main `6a70913590d8eab63320da4f3ce70976c9192500` on 2026-10-12. Lifetime-only head: `b28caf2b39776cf88e238e66a8dff5a945866512`. macOS, Python 3.12.14, Torch 2.13.0, pytest 9.1.1.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/worker tests/v1/worker/test_encoder_runner.py -q
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/core tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD)
git diff --check HEAD~1 HEAD
```

- Encoder runner: **21 passed**.
- Core regression: **252 passed**, with one setup error because `--confcutdir` excluded the upstream `caplog_vllm` logging fixture. Reusing the two unchanged logging fixtures from `tests/conftest.py` in an external pytest plugin, the failed upstream test and lifetime-related selection passed: **15 passed, 198 deselected**. The three core files therefore have 253 distinct passing tests across these invocations.
- Changed-file pre-commit, including Ruff, mypy, Markdown, SPDX and Buildkite test tethering: passed. Whitespace checks: passed.
- Remote CI: [pre-run-check](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/38218309254/job/114708164768) stops before running hooks because the author has 2 merged PRs and the gate requires 4 or a qualifying label. [Read the Docs](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35085948/) also stops at its pre-run check because that gate failed; documentation compilation did not run.

`--confcutdir` avoids the root accelerator-cleanup fixture on macOS. For the logging-fixture retry, copy `temporary_enable_log_propagate` and `caplog_vllm` unchanged from `tests/conftest.py` into `upstream_logging_fixtures.py` outside the checkout (with `import pytest`), then run:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/path/to/fixtures:. VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p upstream_logging_fixtures --confcutdir=tests/v1/core tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'cpu_encoder_input or free_encoder_inputs or encoder_cache_retained_across_preemption or encoder_cache_recomputed or test_encoder_cache_rejects_mismatched_embed_count' -q
```

Tests cover storage release during a live decoding request, repeated hashes, request isolation, retained metadata and replay data, confirmed consumption/in-flight prefill/lookahead, preemption/resume/abort, and rollback restoration.

**Validation limit:** no new GPU model run was performed after this rebase and split. Previous B200 results exercised lifetime release and COW transport together, on an older base; they do not establish the OOM or performance benefit of this lifetime-only patch.

<details>
<summary>Historical B200 validation of the combined patch</summary>

Previously tested against main `528fa835fd37d0805a824d516e22f88df61a771a` with Kimi-K3 on two 8-GPU B200 nodes: TP8 × PP2, DCP8/a2a, EP/deepep_v2, `deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `VLLM_KIMI_K3_SHARD_SP_SHARED_EXPERT=1`, MRV2, `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`, max sequences 192, batched tokens 8192, model length 1048576, FP8 KV, GPU utilization 0.92, no speculative decoding. Python wheel rebuilt using the matching native wheel (`VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`).

Both arms had a 1700 GiB CPU cgroup cap, swap disabled, and 256 GiB `/dev/shm` within that budget. Mooncake used a 128 GiB global segment plus 4 GiB buffer per worker. Only the combined candidate enabled COW shared input storage.

| Workload | Baseline | Combined release + sharing |
|---|---|---|
| Single/four distinct/four repeated/sixteen images; two runs each | 8 completed | Token IDs, logprobs, messages and usage exactly match |
| Prefix repeat | 32768 cached tokens | 32768 cached tokens |
| Forced preemption/resume | One actual preemption; 2048 output tokens | One actual preemption; 2048 output tokens |
| Cancellation | Request state drained | Request state drained |
| 64 concurrent × 16 images × 1024 output tokens | 64/64; 362.43 s; first-node peak 1193.35 GiB | 64/64; 341.47 s; first-node peak 1132.48 GiB |
| 192 requests × 36 images × 16384 output tokens | Kernel-confirmed CPU memcg OOM at 1700 GiB | 192/192; 2959.14 s; first-node peak 1312.495 GiB |
| Four image cases after stress, fresh cache salts | Reference outputs | Token IDs, logprobs and messages exactly match |

The combined candidate completed 3,145,728 output tokens. At an observed 192-running-request decode snapshot, all eight first-node workers retained zero bytes of raw CPU image tensors. Shared inodes were mapped by all eight workers; final image mappings were empty on both nodes. Second-node peak: 1107.800 GiB.

Baseline initially admitted 176 requests; 16 uploads failed on stale keep-alive connections and were replayed on fresh connections before OOM (last sampled running count 181). Candidate used fresh connections for all 192. Request-body hashes matched. Both arms returned HTTP 500 from `reset_prefix_cache?reset_running_requests=true` due to remaining remote-KV references; actual preemption/resume and response completion passed. Timings are single runs, not a stable speedup claim. Synthetic image regression is not a general accuracy benchmark. GPU validation did not cover separate ablations, KV-load rollback, speculative decoding, address-only SHM processor caching, or cross-node TP sharing.

</details>

## Details

MRV2 `EncoderCache.mm_features` previously retained the raw inputs for the whole request. The scheduler now emits request-local release indices at a confirmed consumption boundary. Workers install requests and positional metadata first, then replace only the selected feature's `data` with `None`. Copying the feature list and replacing entries preserves EngineCore replay inputs and other occurrences of the same hash, including the uniprocess executor case. GPU encoder-output eviction and model computation are unchanged.

Related-work check: #50871 targets EngineCore input release for resumable sessions; this patch targets ordinary MRV2 worker ownership. #51207 merged the optional tensor arena on 2026-10-09; this PR makes no transport changes and introduces no alternate SHM implementation. The extracted COW transport overlaps the arena and remains a separate design-comparison branch, with no new PR opened. #51349 proposes a paged processor-cache/IPC subsystem; #49462 targets CUDA IPC. Open-PR searches for `multimodal memory`, `encoder input`, `shared tensor`, and `57368 in:body` were repeated before preparing the split.

Design: `docs/design/mm_cpu_input_lifetime.md`. The production diff adds 111 lines and removes 2; the additional lines are focused tests and documentation.

AI assistance was used for implementation, rebase/conflict resolution, tests and PR preparation.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** The scheduler/worker release protocol is separated from transport design; replay ownership and MRV1 behavior are preserved.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** CPU regressions and pre-commit passed; lifetime-only GPU E2E after the split remains outstanding, as documented above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Checks pass; documentation covers ownership and rollback, with no new examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Scope, related work, commands, results, historical combined evidence and validation limits are recorded.
</details>

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for the thorough work — the lifetime analysis and the B200 validation are impressive. One process-level request: could you split this into two PRs?

1. **Early release of consumed MRV2 CPU inputs** — the scheduler/worker release protocol: `scheduler.py` (consumption boundary + reload detection + tracking resets), `sched/output.py` (the two new `SchedulerOutput` fields), `worker/gpu/mm/encoder_cache.py`, `worker/gpu/model_runner.py`, plus the scheduler/encoder-runner tests.
2. **Node-local shared storage** — the COW file-backed transport: `shared_tensor.py`, `shm_broadcast.py`, `multiproc_executor.py`, `envs.py` (`VLLM_MM_INPUT_SHARED_STORAGE_PATH`), and the shm_broadcast tests.

Rationale: the two mechanisms are independently useful and carry different risk profiles. (1) is a correctness-of-lifetime change on the hot scheduling path that reviewers need to scrutinize line by line; (2) is an opt-in transport feature with POSIX-lease subtleties. Splitting makes each reviewable and revertable on its own — and (1) can likely land much faster without the transport design discussion (e.g. the acknowledged overlap with #51207) gating it.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+# CPU multimodal input lifetime
+
+Model Runner V2 keeps the vision encoder's existing tensor-parallel computation.
+This change addresses ownership of its CPU inputs, without changing TP, EP,
+sequence parallelism, encoder batching, or GPU embedding-cache eviction.
+
+## Request-local release
+
+The scheduler sends `SchedulerOutput.free_encoder_input_ids`, a mapping from
+request ID to input indices. An input is eligible once its placeholder end plus
+prefill lookahead is at or before the confirmed computation boundary. That
+boundary excludes both unconfirmed output placeholders and in-flight tokens,
+including asynchronously scheduled prefill. Inputs scheduled for encoding in the
+current step are excluded.
+
+The worker applies the notification after installing new requests and computing
+any initial model-specific positional metadata. Its `EncoderCache` drops the
+selected feature's `data`, while retaining its identifier and placeholder
+metadata. It does not clear all inputs with the same hash, and does not evict
+GPU embeddings.
+
+EngineCore retains its original feature objects for replay. The worker owns a
+separate feature list and replaces entries rather than mutating those objects;
+this also preserves correctness with the uniprocess executor. Preemption and
+new/resumed/streaming request installation reset the scheduler's release tracking.
+If a KV-load failure rewinds a running request without preempting it, a subsequent
+encoder schedule reinstalls any previously released input from EngineCore through
+`restore_encoder_inputs`. These tensors use the existing executor transport.
+Prefix-cache hits are eligible even when no encoder computation was scheduled.
+Model Runner V1 continues to use its existing lifetime policy. Address-only
+`mm_processor_cache_type=shm` handles retain their existing ownership policy;
+EngineCore does not hold replayable pixel tensors for that separate cache/ACK
+protocol. The release protocol targets full tensor inputs (the
+ordinary LRU processor cache or disabled processor caching).
+
+## Validation
+
+CPU tests cover confirmed consumption, speculative lookahead, in-flight prefill,
+repeated hashes, request-local release, prefix-style reinstalls, synchronous and
+asynchronous preemption/resume, abort, KV-load rollback restoration, and
+preservation of EngineCore replay inputs.
+
+Validate the release protocol with ordinary tensor transport on the same model
+and deterministic request set. Exercise chunked prefill, repeated images, prefix
+hits, forced preemption, cancellation, and long decoding. Compare outputs and
+worker live CPU input bytes while requests are still decoding. Earlier B200
+validation combined this change with optional local sharing; it does not isolate
+the release protocol.

@@ -7550,3 +7550,158 @@ def test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait():
     # Deferring this step alone would ask for 6. The PP wait to 7 stands.
     assert "read" not in scheduler.schedule().num_scheduled_tokens
     assert read.next_decode_eligible_step == 7
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("lookahead", [0, 1, 3])
+def test_cpu_encoder_inputs_release_only_confirmed_consumed_occurrences(lookahead):
+    """Chunking/rollback cannot release a future occurrence of the same hash."""
+    scheduler = Scheduler.__new__(Scheduler)
+    scheduler.use_v2_model_runner = True
+    scheduler.num_prefill_lookahead = lookahead
+    scheduler._released_encoder_input_ids = {}
+    (request,) = create_requests(
+        num_requests=1,
+        num_tokens=64,
+        mm_hashes_list=[["same", "same"]],
+        mm_positions=[
+            [
+                PlaceholderRange(offset=0, length=8),
+                PlaceholderRange(offset=32, length=8),
+            ]
+        ],
+    )
+    req_id = request.request_id
+    scheduler.requests = {req_id: request}
+    request.num_output_placeholders = 4
+    request.num_computed_tokens = 11 + lookahead
+    assert scheduler._get_consumed_encoder_input_ids({req_id: 1}, [], {}) == {}
+    request.num_computed_tokens += 1
+    request.num_in_flight_tokens = request.num_computed_tokens
+    assert scheduler._get_consumed_encoder_input_ids({req_id: 1}, [], {}) == {}
+    request.num_in_flight_tokens = 0
+    assert scheduler._get_consumed_encoder_input_ids({req_id: 1}, [], {}) == {
+        req_id: [0]
+    }
+    assert scheduler._get_consumed_encoder_input_ids({req_id: 1}, [], {}) == {}
+    assert all(feature.data is not None for feature in request.mm_features)
+    # A resumed or streaming request reinstalls all inputs, including a prefix hit.
+    new_request = SimpleNamespace(req_id=req_id)
+    assert scheduler._get_consumed_encoder_input_ids(
+        {req_id: 1}, [new_request], {}
+    ) == {req_id: [0]}
+    request.num_computed_tokens = 44 + lookahead
+    # Never clear an input that this very step needs to encode.
+    assert (
+        scheduler._get_consumed_encoder_input_ids({req_id: 1}, [], {req_id: [1]}) == {}
+    )
+    assert scheduler._get_consumed_encoder_input_ids({req_id: 1}, [], {}) == {
+        req_id: [1]
+    }
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("async_scheduling", [False, True])
+def test_cpu_encoder_input_release_schedule_resume_and_abort(async_scheduling):
+    """Exercise SchedulerOutput events and their reset on preemption/abort."""
+    import time
+
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(
+        model="llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf",
+        use_v2_model_runner=True,
+        async_scheduling=async_scheduling,
+    )
+    (request,) = create_requests(
+        num_requests=1,
+        num_tokens=200,
+        mm_positions=[[PlaceholderRange(offset=0, length=100)]],
+    )
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+    first = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert first.free_encoder_input_ids == {}
+    # Model finished prefill, but the request is still decoding.
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        first,
+        ModelRunnerOutput(
+            req_ids=[request.request_id],
+            req_id_to_index={request.request_id: 0},
+            sampled_token_ids=[[1]],
+            logprobs=None,
+            prompt_logprobs_dict={},
+            pooler_output=[],
+        ),
+    )
+    second = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert second.free_encoder_input_ids == {request.request_id: [0]}
+    scheduler.running.remove(request)
+    scheduler._preempt_request(request, time.monotonic())
+    assert request.request_id not in scheduler._released_encoder_input_ids
+    # Drain the old in-flight decode before the scheduler can resume this request.
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        second,
+        ModelRunnerOutput(
+            req_ids=[request.request_id],
+            req_id_to_index={request.request_id: 0},
+            sampled_token_ids=[[2]],
+            logprobs=None,
+            prompt_logprobs_dict={},
+            pooler_output=[],
+        ),
+    )
+    resumed = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert resumed.free_encoder_input_ids == {}
+    assert resumed.scheduled_new_reqs[0].mm_features[0].data is not None
+    scheduler.finish_requests(request.request_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+    assert request.request_id not in scheduler._released_encoder_input_ids
+
+
+def test_cpu_encoder_input_rollback_reinstalls_only_released_input():
+    """A failed KV load can rewind a running request without preempting it."""
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.mm.encoder_cache import EncoderCache
+
+    scheduler = Scheduler.__new__(Scheduler)
+    scheduler.use_v2_model_runner = True
+    scheduler.num_prefill_lookahead = 0
+    scheduler._released_encoder_input_ids = {}
+    (request,) = create_requests(
+        num_requests=1,
+        num_tokens=64,
+        mm_positions=[[PlaceholderRange(offset=0, length=8)]],
+    )
+    req_id = request.request_id
+    scheduler.requests = {req_id: request}
+    cache = EncoderCache()
+    cache.add_request(req_id, request.mm_features)
+    request.num_computed_tokens = 16
+    released = scheduler._get_consumed_encoder_input_ids({req_id: 1}, [], {})
+    cache.free_encoder_inputs(req_id, released[req_id])
+    assert cache.mm_features[req_id][0].data is None
+    request.num_computed_tokens = 0
+    restored = scheduler._get_encoder_input_reloads({req_id: [0]})
+    cache.restore_encoder_inputs(req_id, restored[req_id])
+    assert cache.mm_features[req_id][0].data is request.mm_features[0].data
+    assert scheduler._get_encoder_input_reloads({req_id: [0]}) == {}
+    request.num_computed_tokens = 16
+    assert scheduler._get_consumed_encoder_input_ids({req_id: 1}, [], {}) == {
+        req_id: [0]
+    }

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for the thorough work — the lifetime analysis and the B200 validation are impressive. One process-level request: could you split this into two PRs?

1. **Early release of consumed MRV2 CPU inputs** — the scheduler/worker release protocol: `scheduler.py` (consumption boundary + reload detection + tracking resets), `sched/output.py` (the two new `SchedulerOutput` fields), `worker/gpu/mm/encoder_cache.py`, `worker/gpu/model_runner.py`, plus the scheduler/encoder-runner tests.
2. **Node-local shared storage** — the COW file-backed transport: `shared_tensor.py`, `shm_broadcast.py`, `multiproc_executor.py`, `envs.py` (`VLLM_MM_INPUT_SHARED_STORAGE_PATH`), and the shm_broadcast tests.

Rationale: the two mechanisms are independently useful and carry different risk profiles. (1) is a correctness-of-lifetime change on the hot scheduling path that reviewers need to scrutinize line by line; (2) is an opt-in transport feature with POSIX-lease subtleties. Splitting makes each reviewable and revertable on its own — and (1) can likely land much faster without the transport design discussion (e.g. the acknowledged overlap with #51207) gating it.
